info.name: AstraKa API
info.description: End-to-end story through every AstraKa API endpoint, in Collection Runner order: anonymous zodiac/horoscope lookups, onboarding, Exercises CRUD, a Course built day by day, publishing, a Cohort (Constellation), a Wanderer's enrollment, reports (own course + a seeded one as Oracle), then cleanup. Re-runnable: names that must be unique use {{$timestamp}}. See docs/postman/README.md for how to get the three bearer tokens and how to grant the Oracle role. Cleanup never touches seeded reference data (zodiac signs, seeded Starshepherds/courses) - only entities this run created itself; a couple of deletes are deliberately left to fail with 409 because the API's own business rules block them (an enrolled Cohort, a Course with a Cohort) - that is the point being demonstrated, not a bug in the collection.

auth.description: This OAuth2 config exists only so the collection's own Authorization tab can show 'Get New Access Token'. No request in this collection inherits it - every folder/request sets its own Bearer auth explicitly against wandererToken/starshepherdToken/oracleToken. Click 'Get New Access Token' once per account (prompt=login forces Auth0's login screen every time, so you can log in as a different one of your three test accounts each click), then copy the resulting access token into the matching variable's CURRENT value - see docs/postman/README.md. If the audience/prompt extra params don't survive import on your Postman version, add them manually under the Authorization tab's advanced/additional parameters.

10. Cleanup
item.description: Deletes everything this run created that the API's business rules allow. The enrolled cohort and its course are deliberately left behind - deleting them is blocked by design (409), which is itself part of what this folder demonstrates. Seeded reference data (zodiac signs, seeded Starshepherds/courses) is never touched by this collection at all.
